key_decisions.decision: Retains Israel and the heart qualification rather than emending to the upright.
Reads both qere verbs as the poet's threatened fall.
Retains the written reference to their death; flags the difficult claim in a note.
Keeps the bodily image instead of replacing eyes with iniquity.
Follows the qere turn; leaves his referent unsettled and notes the obscure water image.
Retains plural sanctuaries and interprets their end without adding an afterlife scheme.
Retains the dream and image analogy; notes the difficult when-you-rise expression.
Preserves receive and honor/glory without making the destination explicit.
Keeps rock and portion as distinct images amid bodily failure.
Renders the sexual infidelity metaphor as covenantal unfaithfulness, noted explicitly.
Retains both divine designations and the final turn from his refuge to your works.
